transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-02-14 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~46 minutes | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood Solutions), Maya Chen (Atlas SecOps), Carlos Ruiz (Atlas Platform), Liam O'Neill (Atlas CISO)

Summary:
- Focus: audit logs and admin activity logging for Redwood Private/Dedicated (what events are captured, export options, retention, encryption/KMS, SSO/RBAC interactions).
- Actionable items: share log schema, schedule SIEM integration walkthrough, confirm retention needs.

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Jordan from Redwood, i'll kick us off. we have priya our se and samir from solutions. quick confirm on roles?
00:12 Maya: maya here, secops at atlas health, i'm leading the compliance part.
00:15 Carlos: carlos platform, i'll be doing the integration work.
00:18 Liam: liam, ciso, i'll chime in on policy / retention reqs.
00:22 Jordan: great. objective today is narrow — audit logs and admin activity, what we capture, how you can export them to your SIEM or S3, retention windows, and encryption options. also how these tie to RBAC/SSO events.
00:38 Priya: i'll jump in on technicals — how logs are structured and flow. quick note, transcript may mis-hear some acronyms like K-M-S or K V cache, sorry if that shows up later.
00:48 Maya: perfect. first question — at a high level what admin events are captured? we need role changes, api key creation, token rotation, and model access, basically all admin ops.
00:58 Priya: totally — Redwood captures admin activity: user provisioning and deprovisioning, SSO/SAML assertions, RBAC role grants/revokes, API key lifecycle (create, rotate, revoke), service account usage, canary and rollout changes, model version pin/unpin, and dedicated node / instance modifications. we also log system-level events like autoscale triggers but those are more infra-level.
01:20 Carlos: do logs include the content of requests? we have PHI concerns.
01:25 Priya: by default we log metadata about requests: request id, user id (redacted where appropriate), model id, sequence length, latency, status codes, and the event type. for hosts with content logging enabled (enterprise opt-in) we can include prompts/responses but we recommend redaction. we offer automatic PII redaction rules and configurable field-level redaction so you can omit or hash user-provided text before it lands in logs.
01:52 Liam: okay, need that clearly documented — regulators will ask. what's the default retention?
01:58 Jordan: default for hosted is 90 days for most audit logs. for Dedicated/Private you can configure retention — enterprise customers commonly request 1 year, 3 years, or legal 7 year WORM style. we support both shorter and extended retention, and we have pricing tiers for long-term storage.
02:18 Maya: and how do exports work? we want to push to our SIEM (splunk) and also a central S3 bucket with SSE-KMS.
02:24 Priya: supported export options: push to Splunk via HEC, Datadog logs ingest, direct delivery to customer S3 or GCS buckets, streaming to Kinesis or Pub/Sub, and BigQuery sinks. Exports are JSONL (newline-delimited JSON) and schema is stable but we do iterate — we'll send you the schema with example events. for S3 delivery we support server-side encryption SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS and you can supply your own customer-managed KMS key for encryption at rest.
02:57 Carlos: can we do real-time streaming to our SIEM? we have alerts that need low latency.
03:02 Priya: yes, SIEM HEC or Kinesis gives near-real-time delivery; expect typical delays in the 1-5s range under normal load. there are batching buffers for throughput but we expose a low-latency path for audit/admin events.
03:19 Maya: audit log integrity — can we enforce immutability / WORM? auditors ask for tamper-evidence.
03:25 Jordan: for Private deployments you can enable WORM semantics on the destination (S3 Object Lock) and we can retain tamper-evidence with checksums. across the platform we compute signed digests of log batches and timestamps; we can provide those digests to you on request for integrity verification.
03:43 Liam: KMS question — do you support customer-managed keys for logs and for any exported artifacts?
03:48 Priya: yes. we support customer-managed keys (CMK) for encryption at rest for both logs stored on Redwood and for S3 exports. in Private deployments you can integrate with your KMS/HSM. note: key rotation is supported but you need to coordinate for previously encrypted archives — we include key IDs in the metadata.
04:06 Carlos: where are logs stored? data residency for EU PHI is a concern.
04:10 Jordan: regionally isolated storage is available; for Redwood Private you control the region, for Dedicated we can shard logs to a customer's preferred AWS region. hosted defaults to regional storage per account with options for EU/US/APAC regions. we'll capture residency in the schema.
04:26 Maya: does the audit log include admin UI actions (console clicks) or only API events?
04:31 Priya: both. UI actions are logged as admin events — user id, action, resource, timestamp, and client ip. it's stitched to the same request ids where possible so you can correlate UI action to API calls.
04:44 Carlos: how do logs tie to SSO events? want to link SAML assertion and session id.
04:49 Priya: SSO events include the assertion id, authn context, identity provider (IdP) metadata, SAML response status, and session creation/termination. we log session start/end and map session ids to subsequent API calls in the audit logs. if your IdP sends context (like device id) we can capture that in attributes.
05:10 Liam: RBAC — we need an auditable trail: who changed roles, who approved, timestamps.
05:14 Priya: yes role grant/revoke includes prev/new role, actor, reason (if provided), and approval metadata if you're using our built-in approver flow. approvals are recorded with approver id and timestamp.
05:26 Jordan: quick interjection — sometimes transcript will show 'KV cache' as K V cache or similar, just ignore transcription quirks.
05:33 Maya: noted. for privacy, is there an option to hash identifiers so logs don't leak user PII?
05:39 Priya: yep — we can apply deterministic hashing to identifiers (like email -> sha256) so you can still correlate but not expose raw PII. you can also configure tiered access so only certain roles can request raw logs.
05:52 Carlos: what's the log format like — sample fields?
05:56 Priya: typical event: timestamp, event_type, request_id, actor_id, actor_email (hashed if configured), resource (model_id, route), action (create_api_key, rotate_key, role_change), outcome (success/fail), latency_ms, region, node_id, and optional payload (truncated request metadata). we'll send a full schema sample.
06:16 Maya: do you support GDPR right-to-be-forgotten on logs?
06:20 Jordan: good question — logs are treatment for operational telemetry. we support targeted redaction and deletion for customer-supplied data on Private/Dedicated deployments. for hosted, we have processes to delete or redact logs on request but it depends on retention policies and legal holds. we recommend using hashing instead of storing raw PII in logs.
06:39 Liam: any differences between audit logs and request traces for debugging?
06:43 Priya: audit logs are security-focused — admin actions, auth, config changes. request traces are deeper app-level traces including token-level cost and per-token latencies. we keep traces for a shorter time by default, but you can configure retention. both are linkable via request_id.
07:02 Carlos: export transformations — can we enrich logs with internal fields before shipping to SIEM?
07:07 Priya: yes you can configure pipelines to add tags, environment, or customer fields. we support adding Enrichments at export time and applying regex/pattern replacements. we also support sending to an intermediate S3 where you run glue jobs before ingestion.
07:23 Maya: audit log alerting — do you provide built-in alerts for suspicious admin activity?
07:28 Jordan: Redwood Console has rule-based alerts (e.g., sudden spike in api key rotates, large export volumes, role change outside business hours). we also expose events to your SIEM so you can build richer correlation rules.
07:42 Carlos: about retention costs — you mentioned pricing tiers?
07:45 Jordan: yes longer retention and WORM storage have additional costs; we'll provide a pricing sheet. for many customers we setup lifecycle to move older logs to cheaper object storage after X days.
07:59 Priya: quick technical note — we emit logs in JSON schema v1 with a version field so parsing is stable across schema updates. we publish changelogs and deprecation windows.
08:14 Maya: regulatory ask — for SOC 2/ISO audits we need attestations and sample logs, can you provide those?
08:20 Jordan: we can provide SOC 2 report and ISO documentation under NDA, and sample anonymized logs and integrity digests for audit. we'll share links in the follow-up.
08:34 Liam: how do you handle service account keys that may be compromised — is there an automated detection?
08:40 Priya: we have anomaly detection flags (unusual geo, high volume, odd hours) and can trigger alerts. compromised key flows should be revoked and events are recorded with actor and affected resources.
08:50 Carlos: is there an API to pull logs programmatically?
08:53 Priya: yes — export endpoints and a logs retrieval API for shorter windows. for bulk long-term access we recommend S3/GCS export.
08:59 Maya: does the platform capture who requested a model rollback or canary promotion? that's important for our change control.
09:05 Priya: yes those change control actions are audit events with actor id, old/new versions, and rollout percentage.
09:12 Jordan: circling back — examples of admin events we capture: create/delete user, role assignment, password reset, SSO config change, audit export requested, api key ops, model pin, rollback, node lifecycle events.
09:26 Maya: excellent. do you support federated logs so we can keep them on-prem?
09:30 Priya: for Private deployments yes, logs can be kept on your on-prem storage; for Dedicated we can push to your VPC-owned S3 or customer-managed storage.
09:40 Carlos: is there a documented retention policy per event type? like auth events retained 365 days, request traces 90 days, admin events 7 years?
09:48 Jordan: we provide defaults but it's configurable per customer. many customers choose long-term retention only for admin events and keep traces shorter. we'll include sample policy templates.
09:59 Maya: what about access controls to logs inside Redwood — RBAC scoping?
10:03 Priya: logs are access-controlled — roles determine who can view raw logs, who can request exports, and who can manage retention. there is an audit on log access itself — when someone retrieves logs we log that retrieval as an admin event.
10:18 Liam: do you have MFA enforced for console admins?
10:21 Jordan: MFA is enforced for all privileged Redwood accounts; for your users we integrate with IdP enforced MFA via SAML.
10:30 Carlos: any limits on schema size or event size?
10:33 Priya: events are capped (we'll provide exact byte limits) but we provide truncation and payload references — large payloads can be stored in object storage with references in the log.
10:46 Maya: curious about correlation ids — do you have a single request_id across UI/API/background jobs?
10:50 Priya: yes we propagate a global trace id in many flows; background jobs reference the originating request when available.
11:02 Jordan: small tangent — auditing of changes to retention and export configurations is also logged. so if someone alters S3 bucket destination it's an auditable event.
11:12 Carlos: operational question: for SIEM integration, any recommended best practices?
11:16 Priya: we recommend pushing enriched JSONL to a staging S3 and running a normalization job before ingesting to Splunk; use the request_id and actor hash for correlation, and set ACLs on the S3 bucket with least privilege. we can provide a playbook.
11:32 Maya: are there examples of ACL templates or terraform for S3 buckets?
11:36 Jordan: yes, we'll share terraform snippets and IAM policy templates in the follow-up.
11:44 Liam: legal will ask about subpoenas / legal holds — can you put holds on logs?
11:48 Jordan: yes for Private/Dedicated we can support legal holds and exclude specific archives from lifecycle deletion. for hosted we have processes to retain or export logs to satisfy legal holds but need coordination.
12:02 Carlos: question on performance — do log exports impact inference latency?
12:07 Priya: no, logs are emitted asynchronously; export pipelines are decoupled. there is a small CPU/memory overhead for event generation but it's designed to be non-blocking so inference latency isn't affected under normal conditions.
12:21 Maya: can you provide a sample event for role change and for api key rotation?
12:26 Priya: yes we'll send samples; they include event_type, actor, target_resource, timestamps, and metadata including IP and region.
12:34 Jordan: (brief pause) we should talk about retention costs and accounting for storage — we'll provide price bands.
12:41 Priya: also, for compliance we can enable periodic export to your long-term archive.
12:47 Maya: anything else on encryption in transit? we need mTLS to our SIEM endpoint.
12:51 Priya: we support TLS 1.2/1.3 for all endpoints and mTLS for S3 or collector endpoints where required. for Splunk HEC we support token+TLS and can support mTLS for dedicated connectors.
13:05 Carlos: do you capture IP addresses and can they be masked/removed?
13:08 Priya: yes IPs are captured by default for admin events and we can mask or omit them on export if you have privacy concerns.
13:16 Maya: is there log sampling anywhere that could drop important audit events?
13:20 Jordan: audit/admin events are not sampled; we may sample high-volume request traces but audit trail is preserved at full fidelity.
13:31 Carlos: how about retention for export buckets — lifecycle is customer-managed?
13:34 Priya: yes once delivered to your S3 it's under your lifecycle control. we recommend lifecycle policies and MFA-delete for critical archives.
13:45 Maya: can you sign shared secrets for HEC endpoints? we need rotation guidance.
13:49 Priya: yes we support rotating tokens and can provide rotation playbooks. tokens are logged as events when rotated but not exposed in logs.
13:58 Liam: wrap up — i'd like to see the schema and an NDA copy for SOC2 artifacts.
14:04 Jordan: we'll get that over. next steps are in the action items. anything else?
14:10 Maya: no, this was good. thanks.

(Conversation continues with some small clarifications and scheduling)

43:00 Jordan: final recap — i'll send SOC2/ISO docs link, audit log schema, terraform snippets for S3 and IAM, pricing bands for retention, and priya will run SIEM integration demo next week. maya will confirm retention window.
43:20 Maya: yep. thanks.
43:25 Carlos: thanks everyone.
43:30 Liam: thanks.

End of transcript.
